sealed_candidate.answer: ## Decision-support answer: Which productivity outcome and comparison should drive the decision? (Fixture: Aster Enterprise, FICTIONAL ASTER ENTERPRISE FIXTURE labels on both sources; treated as the current record per instructions, not as real-world measurements.)### Declared outcome (per policy, [measurement-policy])The decision-relevant outcome is **agent-assisted delivery evaluated on matched tasks**, measured as a composite that must include:- **Quality gates** (pass/fail against defined quality criteria)- **Human review time**- **Rework** (post-acceptance corrections)- **Elapsed lead time**- **Total cost**, and **counting failed or abandoned tasks**The policy explicitly prohibits inferring causal benefit from accepted-PR counts ([measurement-policy]).### Required comparisonPer the policy, the comparison must be **matched tasks** — equivalent task classes assessed with and without agent assistance (or otherwise matched), under a declared **accounting boundary** covering reviewer hours, failure counts, and provider costs ([measurement-policy]).### What the pilot note provides — and why it cannot drive the decisionThe pilot note reports only **40 accepted pull requests in one month**, with **no task mix, control group, reviewer hours, failure count, or provider costs** ([measurement-context]). This fails every element of the declared outcome: no quality-gate results, no review-time or rework data, no lead time, no cost, no failed/abandoned task counts, and no matched baseline.### Missing elements that must be exposed before any conclusion (obligation, role=implementation_evidence, weight=5)The following are **unresolved** on the supplied record:- **Outcome definition in practice**: the pilot measures only accepted-PR volume; the policy-required composite outcome (quality, review time, rework, lead time, cost, failures) was not measured.- **Baseline / matched comparison**: no control group or matched-task comparison exists.- **Task mix**: unknown; 40 PRs cannot be interpreted without knowing task classes and difficulty.- **Accounting boundary**: reviewer hours and provider costs are absent, so total cost is unknown.- **Time horizon**: one month is the only period stated; no declared evaluation window or horizon consistent with the policy's matched-task design.Contradiction note: the pilot's implicit framing (accepted PRs = productivity) directly conflicts with the policy's explicit prohibition on inferring causal benefit from accepted-PR counts. The contradiction is preserved: the policy governs; the pilot note does not satisfy it ([measurement-policy] vs. [measurement-context]).### Clarifying question (blocking)Since **Productive** is undefined in the pilot and the accepted-PR count lacks a comparison, the blocking question stands:**Which outcome, baseline, task class, and time period should define 'productive'?**### Decision recommendation**Abstain from concluding agent productivity** on the current record. The decision should be driven by the policy-defined composite outcome on matched tasks with a declared accounting boundary; the supplied pilot supplies none of these. Until a matched comparison with quality, review-time, rework, lead-time, cost, and failure accounting exists, the 40-PR figure is not evidence of productivity and cannot support the decision.### Limits of the supplied evidence- The source pack is a fictional fixture; it establishes the **required measurement design** but contains **no real measurements**.- No independent publishers are available or required (minimum: 0); both sources are internal fixture records.- The evidence cannot establish whether agent assistance produced any benefit; that obligation remains **unresolved** until the declared outcome, matched comparison, and accounting boundary are implemented.
